one_liner: Feature flags that go through pull-request review like the rest of your code, evaluated at the edge in under 5ms.
description: togglr treats flag changes as code: every toggle, rollout percentage change, and environment override is a diff in a Git-backed config that goes through PR review, with full history and instant rollback. Evaluation happens at the edge in under 5 milliseconds p99. Open-source SDKs for the major languages, hosted control plane for teams.
target_user: Product engineering teams that ship behind flags

icp.who: Engineering teams of 5-50 at product companies practicing trunk-based development
icp.pain: Flag dashboards drift with no review trail — one misclicked toggle in a web UI can take production down with zero record of who changed what
icp.buying_trigger: A flag-related incident with no audit trail, or a LaunchDarkly renewal quote that triggers a search for alternatives

differentiators: Flag changes are pull requests: reviewed, attributed, revertable with git
Sub-5ms p99 evaluation at the edge via Cloudflare Workers
Open-source SDKs — no proprietary client lock-in
proof_points: p99 edge evaluation latency under 5ms, benchmark published in docs
SDK repos have a combined 900 GitHub stars
Every flag change in the demo org is a browsable pull request
pricing_current: freemium (free up to 5 seats and 1M evaluations/month, then $8/seat)

voice.sample_phrase: Your last outage was a toggle nobody reviewed. Fix that.

confidence.notes: Workflow differentiation is concrete and demoable. Latency benchmark is vendor-published.
